core_obligations: Induct on the number of primes, picking a homogeneous element of positive degree in I avoiding the first r - 1 of them (proof lines 13856-13859).

If that element already avoids the last prime, finish; otherwise use that the product of the first r - 1 primes with I is not contained in the last prime, and take a homogeneous witness y outside it (proof lines 13860-13864).
Combine the two elements with exponents given by their degrees, which is again homogeneous of positive degree and avoids every prime (proof line 13864).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case of no inclusions among the primes and induct on their number (proof lines 13855-13859).
Build the avoiding element as a binomial combination of two homogeneous witnesses with swapped degree exponents (proof lines 13860-13865).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a graded ideal I contained in the positive-degree part and not contained in any of finitely many homogeneous primes contains a homogeneous element of positive degree avoiding all of them (statement lines 13846-13853). The proof does not reduce to the general prime avoidance lemma: it inducts on the number of primes, and in the critical case where the previously chosen homogeneous element lies in the last prime it uses that I times the product of the other primes is not contained in the last prime, takes a homogeneous witness, and combines the two witnesses as x to the degree of y plus y to the degree of x (proof lines 13855-13865). That swap of exponents is the step that makes the result homogeneous, and the author displays it. H2.
